analist-1.title: SQL and Fundamentals
q: What is the difference between INNER JOIN and LEFT JOIN? When do you use each?
INNER matches: match, intersect, both tables
LEFT keeps all: left, all, null
Example use: for example, customer, order

INNER JOIN returns only the rows that match in both tables. LEFT JOIN returns every row from the left table, with NULLs on the right side when there is no match. For example, I use LEFT JOIN to find customers who have never placed an order.
Explain the difference between the mean and the median, and when each can be misleading.
Definitions: middle, sum, divid
Outliers: outlier, extreme
Skewed distributions: skew, distribution, salary, income

The mean is the sum of all values divided by their count; the median is the middle of the sorted data. Outliers pull the mean, so for skewed distributions such as income the median is more representative.

analist-2.title: Analysis Cases
q: The app's daily active users dropped 15% last week. How do you analyze it?
Validate the data: tracking, data error, validat, verif
Segmentation: segment, platform, country, breakdown
External factors: holiday, season, competitor, external
Internal changes: release, version, campaign, change
Hypotheses: hypothes, assum

First I check that the data is correct, with no tracking error. Then I break the drop down by platform, country and new versus returning users to see where it is concentrated. I form hypotheses about releases, campaigns and holidays and test them with data.
How do you make sure an A/B test result is reliable?
Sample size: sample, power
Statistical significance: p-value, p value, significan, confidence interval
Duration / peeking: duration, early, week, peek
Random assignment: random

Before the test I calculate the required sample size and duration, and I don't stop early after peeking at results. I check that assignment is random and the groups are balanced. I interpret the result with the p-value and confidence interval, together with the business impact.

analist-3.title: Stakeholder Management
q: A manager wants a conclusion in the report that the data doesn't support. What do you do?
Understand the goal: why, understand, goal
Show it with data: data, chart, show
Offer an alternative: alternative, suggest, different
Honesty: honest, ethic, transparen

First I try to understand the manager's real goal. I show clearly, with a chart, what the data says and stay transparent. Then I suggest an alternative story or extra analysis that serves the goal and is supported by the data.

bi-1.title: Dashboards
q: How do you design a good dashboard?
Audience: user, audience, who
Few, focused metrics: few, focus, important
Right chart type: chart, line, bar
Context / comparison: target, previous, compar

First I clarify who will use the dashboard and for which decision. I focus on a few critical metrics, using line charts for trends and bar charts for comparisons. I give each metric context by comparing it with a target or the previous period.
What is a star schema?
Fact table: fact
Dimension tables: dimension
Reporting speed: fast, performance, query
Example: sales, customer, product
A fact table in the middle holds measurable events (for example sales), surrounded by dimension tables that describe them (customer, product, date). It enables fast reporting with simple joins.

bi-2.title: Data Consistency
q: The revenue figures in two different reports don't match. How do you investigate?
Definition differences: definition, return, tax
Filters / dates: filter, date, time zone
Data source: source, table
Single source of truth: single source, standard, dictionary

First I compare how each report defines revenue (are returns and tax included?). I check the date filters and time zone, and which tables feed each report. Finally I tie the metric to a single definition in a shared data dictionary.

bilimci-1.title: ML Fundamentals
q: What is overfitting and how do you prevent it?
Definition: training, memoriz, generaliz
Validation: validation, cross
Regularization: regulariz, l1, l2, dropout
Data / simpler model: data, simpl

Overfitting happens when a model memorizes the training data and can't generalize to new data. I measure it with cross-validation and prevent it with regularization (L1/L2), dropout, a simpler model or more data.
Can you explain the difference between precision and recall with an example?
Precision: precision
Recall: recall, sensitiv, catch
Trade-off: trade, balance, threshold
Example: for example, spam, cancer, fraud

Precision is how many of the cases we call positive are actually positive; recall is how many of the real positives we catch. For example, recall is more critical in cancer screening and precision in a spam filter. The threshold sets this balance.

bilimci-2.title: Modeling Case
q: You're going to build a customer churn model. What are your steps?
Problem definition: defin, churn, target
Feature engineering: feature
Model and evaluation: model, metric, auc
Business action: action, campaign, business

First I define churn precisely (for example, 30 days without activity). I build features such as usage frequency and complaints, and evaluate the model with AUC and precision/recall. The real value comes from tying it to a business action, such as a targeted campaign for at-risk customers.

pm-1.title: Product Thinking
q: Pick your favorite app. How would you improve it?
User segment: user, segment, persona
Problem: problem, issue, need
Proposed solution: feature, solution, propos
Success metric: metric, measure, rate, kpi
I pick a target user segment and define their biggest problem. I prioritize two or three solution ideas by impact and effort. I measure success with something like the weekly repeat-use rate.
How do you prioritize a list of features?
Framework: rice, moscow, impact, effort
Link to goals: goal, strategy, okr
Data / feedback: data, feedback, user

First I look at how each item connects to company goals. I score reach, impact, confidence and effort with a framework such as RICE. I validate the scores with user feedback and data, and share the result transparently with stakeholders.

pm-2.title: Metrics
q: Which metrics would you use to measure the success of a food delivery app?
North star metric: north star, main metric
Acquisition: acquisition, new user, download
Retention: retention, repeat
Revenue / basket: revenue, basket, per order
Counter-metrics: delivery time, cancel, complaint, satisfaction

As the north star I choose completed orders per week. I support it with acquisition, 30-day repeat orders and basket size. To protect quality I track delivery time and cancellation rate as counter-metrics.

pm-3.title: Strategy
q: The company wants to enter a new market (for example Germany). How do you decide?
Market size: market, size
Competition: competitor, competition
Localization: local, language, regulat, legal
Pilot: pilot, test, experiment, mvp

I size the market and map the competition. I assess localization costs such as language, payment habits and regulation. Instead of a full launch, I start a pilot in one city and decide based on clear success criteria.

po-1.title: Agile Fundamentals
q: How do you write a good user story?
Format: as a, i want, so that
Acceptance criteria: acceptance, criteria
Small and independent: small, independent, invest
Value: value, benefit
I use the format "As a [user], I want [need], so that [benefit]" and add clear acceptance criteria. I make sure the story is small enough to finish in a sprint, independent and testable (INVEST).
Can you describe the Scrum ceremonies and their purpose?
Sprint planning: planning
Daily stand-up: daily, stand-up, standup
Sprint review: review, demo
Retrospective: retro

In sprint planning the team picks the goal and the work. In the daily stand-up it shares progress and blockers. In the review the finished work is shown to stakeholders for feedback. In the retrospective the team discusses what to change to improve how it works.

po-2.title: Backlog Management
q: An urgent request arrives in the middle of a sprint. What do you do?
Assess the impact: impact, urgen, priorit
Trade-off: remove, instead, swap, trade
Talk to the team: team, discuss, talk
Stakeholder communication: stakeholder, inform

First I assess whether the request is truly urgent and what its impact is. If it is, I talk to the team and take out work of similar size from the sprint. I tell stakeholders about the change and the reason transparently.

ux-1.title: Research
q: Which user research methods do you know?
Interviews: interview
Usability testing: usability, test
Surveys: survey
Analytics: analytics, data, heatmap

On the qualitative side I use user interviews and usability tests to understand the "why". On the quantitative side I measure the "how much" with surveys, product analytics and heatmaps. I pick the method based on the question.
How do you defend a design decision to an unconvinced stakeholder?
User data: user, data, research
Business goal: goal, business, metric
Alternatives: alternative, option
Propose a test: test, a/b

I tie the decision to findings from user research and to the business goal. I show the alternatives I considered and why they were dropped. If we still disagree, I propose trying both options in an A/B test.

ux-2.title: Flow Improvement
q: An app's sign-up flow has a high drop-off rate. How do you improve it?
Funnel analysis: funnel, step, where
Fewer steps: reduc, shorten, social login
User testing: test, observ
Measurement: measure, rate

First I use funnel analysis to find the step where users leave. I observe a few users to understand why. I remove unnecessary fields, add social login and shorten the steps, then measure the effect with the completion rate.

performans-1.title: Fundamentals
q: Which metrics do you use to measure the success of a digital campaign?
Conversion: conversion
Cost: cac, cpa, cost, cpc
Return: roas, roi, return
Chosen by goal: goal, objective, awareness
First I clarify the campaign goal: awareness or sales. For sales I look at conversion rate, acquisition cost (CAC/CPA) and ROAS; for awareness, at reach and recall.

performans-2.title: Campaign Cases
q: How would you launch a new coffee brand with a budget of 50,000 TL?
Target audience: target audience, persona, audience
Channel choice: instagram, tiktok, channel, influencer
Budget split: budget, split, alloca, %
Measurement: measure, metric, test

I define the audience as urban coffee lovers aged 20 to 35. I put 50% of the budget into micro-influencers, 30% into Instagram and TikTok ads and 20% into tasting events. In the first two weeks I test creatives and shift budget based on acquisition cost.
The campaign's ROAS halved in two weeks. What do you do?
Breakdown analysis: campaign, channel, creative, breakdown
Creative fatigue: creative, fatigue, frequency
Targeting: audience, targeting
Measurement issues: tracking, pixel, attribution, measure

First I check that measurement (pixel, attribution) is working correctly. Then I break the drop down by channel, campaign and creative. If frequency is high there is creative fatigue, so I launch new creatives and targeting tests.

icerik-1.title: Content Planning
q: How do you plan a brand's social media content calendar?
Goal / audience: goal, audience
Content pillars: pillar, theme, categor
Frequency / platform: frequen, platform, per week
Measurement: engagement, reach, measure

First I set the goal and the audience. I create three or four content pillars, such as educational, entertaining and product-focused. I set a weekly posting frequency for each platform and update the calendar every month based on engagement and reach.

icerik-2.title: Community & Crisis
q: A post was misunderstood and is drawing backlash. What do you do?
Respond quickly: quick, fast, immediately
Listen / analyze: understand, listen, analy
Apology / transparency: apolog, transparen, statement
Process improvement: process, approval, lesson

I quickly analyze the situation and why people are reacting. If needed I remove the post and publish a sincere, transparent statement or apology. Afterwards I review the content approval process to prevent a similar mistake.

seo-1.title: SEO Fundamentals
q: Can you explain the technical, content and authority (backlink) sides of SEO?
Technical SEO: speed, sitemap, index, technical
Content: keyword, content, intent
Authority: backlink, link, authority
Measurement: search console, ranking, traffic

On the technical side, site speed, the sitemap and indexability matter; for content, pages that match search intent and use keywords naturally; for authority, backlinks from trusted sites. I measure results with Search Console and organic traffic.

seo-2.title: SEO Cases
q: Organic traffic suddenly dropped by 30%. How do you investigate?
Algorithm update: algorithm, update
Technical error: robots, noindex, index, technical
Page-level analysis: page, breakdown, query
Competitors: competitor

First I check whether it coincides with a Google algorithm update. I look for technical errors such as robots.txt, noindex or redirects. In Search Console I find which pages and queries dropped, and look at how competitors are doing on those queries.

b2b-1.title: Sales Fundamentals
q: Sell me this pen.
Asking about needs: question, need, what for, how do you use
Benefit focus: benefit, helps, easy
Handling objections: objection, expensive, price
Closing: close, buy, try, offer

First I ask questions: what do you use a pen for most? Based on the answer I explain the benefit. I handle the price objection by pointing to how long it lasts, and close with a clear offer that makes buying today easy.

b2b-2.title: Negotiation & Pipeline
q: The customer says "Your competitor is 20% cheaper." How do you respond?
Understanding: question, understand, compared to what
Value focus: value, quality, support, total cost
Reciprocal trade: in return, long term, package

First I ask what the comparison covers. I show the total cost of ownership, support and quality with concrete numbers. If a discount is needed, I ask for something in return, such as a longer contract.
How do you manage your sales pipeline?
Stages: stage, funnel
Qualification: qualif, budget, decision maker
CRM: crm, record
Conversion rates: rate, conversion, forecast
I track opportunities through clear stages. I qualify each one by budget, decision maker, need and timing. I record everything in the CRM and forecast sales from the conversion rates between stages.

perakende-1.title: Greeting Customers
q: How do you approach a customer who walks into the store?
Greeting: greet, hello, smile
Asking about needs: question, need
Product suggestion: suggest, recommend, product
Add-on sale: add-on, complementary, cross

I greet them with a smile and give them space without pressure. I use open questions to understand what they're looking for and recommend a product that fits their need. Where it makes sense, I make an add-on sale with a complementary product.

perakende-2.title: Difficult Customers
q: An angry customer wants to return a product, but the return period has passed. What do you do?
Calm listening: listen, calm, empath
Explaining the policy: policy, rule, period
Alternative solution: alternative, exchange, store credit, manager
Winning the customer: satisf, come back

First I listen calmly and show empathy. I explain the return policy politely. I try not to lose the customer by offering alternatives such as an exchange, store credit or an exception approved by a manager.

musteri-1.title: Customer Satisfaction
q: How do you measure customer satisfaction?
NPS: nps
CSAT: csat, satisfaction survey, survey
Feedback: feedback, review, comment
Repeat purchase / churn: repeat, churn, renewal

I measure the likelihood to recommend with NPS and satisfaction with a specific interaction with CSAT. I read open-ended feedback regularly. As the real outcome indicator I track renewal and churn rates.

musteri-2.title: Account Recovery
q: A major customer says they won't renew their contract. What do you do?
Understanding why: why, understand, listen
Showing value: value, gain, report
Solution plan: plan, solution, action
Senior management support: manager, senior, executive

First I listen to understand the real reason. I prepare a report showing the value we have delivered so far in numbers. I present a concrete action plan for the issues and, if needed, bring senior management into the conversation.

muhasebe-1.title: Financial Statements
q: Can you explain the three main financial statements and how they relate to each other?
Income statement: income statement, profit, loss
Balance sheet: balance sheet, asset, liabilit, equity
Cash flow statement: cash flow
Links between them: net income, net profit, link, flow

The income statement shows revenue, expenses and net profit for a period. The balance sheet shows assets, liabilities and equity at a point in time. The cash flow statement shows how cash changed. Net profit flows into equity and is the starting point of the cash flow statement.

muhasebe-2.title: Month-End Close
q: What do you do in the month-end close process?
Reconciliation: reconcil, bank
Accruals / provisions: accrual, provision
Checks: check, verif
Reporting: report
I reconcile bank and current accounts. I record the period's accruals and provisions. I check the trial balance and any unusual movements, then prepare the management reports.

fin-analiz-1.title: Analysis Fundamentals
q: Why might a company that looks profitable run short of cash?
Receivables: receivable, payment terms, collect
Inventory: inventory, stock
Capital expenditure: investment, capex
Accrual vs cash: accrual, cash, difference

Profit is calculated on an accrual basis, while cash comes in only when it's collected. Long payment terms on receivables, growing inventory or large capital expenditure can drain cash even while there is profit. That's why I monitor working capital.

fin-analiz-2.title: Valuation
q: Which methods would you use to value a company?
Discounted cash flow: dcf, discounted cash
Multiples: multiple, p/e, ev/ebitda
Assumptions: assum, growth, discount rate
Sensitivity analysis: sensitiv, scenario

I combine the DCF method, which discounts future cash flows to today at a discount rate, with multiples of similar companies such as P/E and EV/EBITDA. I run a sensitivity analysis on the growth and discount assumptions and present a value range.

denetim-1.title: Internal Control
q: What is internal control and why does it matter?
Segregation of duties: segregation of duties, separate person, different person
Authorization / approval: approv, authoriz
Risk: risk, error, fraud
Example: for example

Internal control means the processes set up to prevent errors and fraud. For example, the person who prepares a payment is different from the one who approves it (segregation of duties), and amounts above a limit need approval. It makes financial reporting reliable.

denetim-2.title: Audit Case
q: You notice an unusual increase in an expense item. How do you investigate?
Analytical review: trend, compar, analytic
Document checks: document, invoice, sample
Interviews: interview, ask, talk
Reporting: report, finding

First I compare the increase with previous periods and the budget. I select a sample and check the invoices and approval documents. I talk to the unit involved to get an explanation, then report the findings and recommendations.

ise-alim-1.title: Recruiting Fundamentals
q: How do you find candidates for a hard-to-fill position?
Clarifying the role: need, hiring manager, profile, requirement
Channels: linkedin, career, channel, job post
Direct outreach: direct, sourcing, message
Referrals: referral, recommend

First I clarify the profile and the must-haves with the hiring manager. Alongside the job post I search LinkedIn directly and reach out to candidates with personalized messages. I also use the employee referral program and industry communities.
What is a competency-based interview?
Defining competencies: competenc, skill
Past behaviour: past, example, experience
Structured questions: structured, same question, standard
Scoring: score, assess, scale

It's a structured interview where you define the competencies critical for the role and, for each one, ask the candidate for concrete examples from their past. Every candidate gets the same questions and the answers are scored on a common scale, which reduces bias.

ise-alim-2.title: Offers & Candidate Experience
q: A candidate you really wanted turned down the offer. What do you do?
Understanding why: why, understand, ask
Room to negotiate: salary, benefit, flexib, remote
Talking to the manager: manager, budget
Keeping the relationship: relationship, contact, future

First I talk to the candidate to understand the real reason. If there's room to negotiate beyond salary, such as flexible working or benefits, I review it with the manager. Even if the answer doesn't change, I keep the relationship good; they may be a candidate again in the future.

ik-is-ortagi-1.title: Employee Relations
q: An employee comes to you with a complaint about their manager. How do you proceed?
Listening / confidentiality: listen, confidential, trust
Gathering information: information, document, example
Impartiality: impartial, neutral, both sides, manager
Follow-up: follow up, action, solution
I listen carefully to the employee in confidence and note concrete examples. Staying neutral, I also get the manager's view. I create a plan to resolve it and then follow up on the situation.

ik-is-ortagi-2.title: Engagement & Performance
q: Employee turnover in a team has risen sharply. How do you analyze it?
Data analysis: data, rate, breakdown
Exit interviews: exit interview, reason
Manager effect: manager, leadership
Action plan: action, plan, salary, career

First I look at the turnover rate broken down by tenure and role. I pull common reasons from exit interviews; often the manager relationship, pay or career growth stands out. Based on the findings I prepare a concrete action plan together with the manager.
